I have been working this land for 30 years. I know what works in Quzhou. My husband and I manage everything ourselves now, so I have to plan around what the two of us can actually do.

My 14 mu is split the way it has always been — I keep about 4 mu for cotton and the other 10 mu runs on the wheat-maize rotation. Cotton brings in the cash income, but it is punishing work and my back is not what it was. I will not expand it.

For **wheat**, I plant in October after I turn the soil over properly with the plough — you need a deep turn to break up the compaction from summer maize. I buy improved variety seeds from the township supply store, the same ones I have used for several years now. I apply base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress at jointing. I will irrigate four times: once before freezing in winter, once at jointing, once at heading, and once when grain is filling. Two rounds of pesticide — one for powdery mildew, one for aphids. I expect around 450 jin per mu, which is normal for my fields.

For **summer maize**, I sow directly into the wheat stubble right after the June harvest — no time to till, the next crop has to go in fast. I use hybrid seed, everyone around here does for maize now. I put the fertilizer in two shots: base and then topdress when the corn is knee-high. Three irrigations if summer rain is poor. I have good well water so I am not worried.

For **cotton**, I start seedbed prep in April. The land gets rotary tillage. I use improved cotton seed — the variety my neighbor has been using that does well against bollworm. Cotton needs the most attention: I spray five times over the season, watching carefully for bollworm in July and August. Four irrigations through the long growing period. I top the plants to control height because I cannot hire extra hands for a jungle of growth.
